questions.q: According to this lesson, what does moving to the cloud change about data governance?
options: The terrain governance operates on, not the underlying principles of decision rights and stewardship
Nothing at all — cloud and on-premises governance are identical in every respect
Governance is no longer necessary because the cloud provider handles it entirely
Only the vocabulary changes; the actual risks are unique to on-premises systems
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit: everything from the Data Governance Foundations course still applies. What changes is the terrain — elastic, API-driven, multi-tenant infrastructure provisioned by anyone with console access.

questions.q: Why does provisioning speed in the cloud create a governance challenge?
options: A storage account or S3 bucket can exist in minutes, often with no procurement or governance review
Cloud providers require a governance review before any resource can be created
It doesn't — provisioning speed has no bearing on governance
Only database resources can be provisioned quickly; storage still requires approval
questions.explain: Anyone with console access and a credit card can spin up storage in minutes, with sensitive data in it shortly after — no ticket, no review, unless policy explicitly prevents it.

questions.q: Why does this course teach Azure and AWS together instead of one cloud at a time?
options: Most organizations are multi-cloud by accumulation, and the underlying governance concepts are the same ideas under different names
AWS and Azure share the exact same console, so there's nothing extra to learn
Azure is being deprecated in favor of AWS, so only the AWS material will remain relevant
Multi-cloud environments are extremely rare and this is mostly a theoretical exercise
questions.explain: Most organizations end up multi-cloud through acquisitions, partnerships, or team choice rather than a deliberate strategy — and identity, hierarchy, policy, and encryption are the same concepts under different names in each.

questions.q: What does "governance has to be expressed as code or policy, not memos" mean in a cloud context?
options: A rule like "encrypt all storage accounts" does nothing unless it's enforced through a policy engine like Azure Policy or AWS Config
Written governance documentation is no longer useful in any cloud environment
Only developers are allowed to write governance policies, never governance staff
Cloud providers automatically convert every written policy into enforced code
questions.explain: A written policy a future engineer can simply skip isn't governance — it's a suggestion. In the cloud, governance needs a policy engine behind it to actually be enforced.

questions.q: Which chapter of this course covers governing data that spans both Azure and AWS at once?
options: Chapter 5, Multi-Cloud Governance
Chapter 1, Cloud Governance Architecture
Chapter 2, Identity and Access
Chapter 3, Storage and Catalogs
questions.explain: The course roadmap closes with Chapter 5, which the lesson describes as "the hardest problem — governing data that spans both clouds at once."
